intro.title: Render Props (MouseTracker)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a MouseTracker component that follows your cursor's position on the screen. You will learn the Render Props pattern, a React technique where a component receives a function as a prop to determine what to render. This involves using TypeScript to define prop types and React's useState and useEffect hooks to manage state and side effects. By the end, you'll understand how to create reusable components that delegate their rendering logic, making your UI more flexible and maintainable.
intro.usecase: The render props pattern is commonly used in real-world UI components that need to share behavior while allowing flexible rendering. For example, in dashboard applications, you might create a `DataFetcher` component that handles API loading states and errors, while letting different dashboard widgets define their own visual layouts for the data. Interactive data tables often use render props to customize cell rendering while the table component manages sorting and pagination logic. This pattern also appears in form libraries where a `Field` component handles validation and state management, but allows developers to render custom input controls. Even tooltip or popover components use render props to inject positioning logic while letting you style the content freely.
